components.name: Regularized Taylor VI prediction
components.operation: Solve the strong VI for U_{p,x_i} exactly, then compute its Bregman-based lambda_i.
components.requires: Exact Definition 3.1 interface; positive step divergence for the displayed negative power.

Approximate solves require separate residual conditions; they are not covered by this exact rule.

content.family: Mirror Prox with regularized Taylor VI prediction and adaptive Bregman weights

limitations.statement: Theorem 3.3 is retained as a lead; its uniform weak-gap bound is not an accepted performance link.
The printed rule lacks an explicit zero-step branch for p>=2. This record restricts its executable scope to positive step divergences and adds no local branch.

limitations.scope: Exact subproblem interface and its computational cost
limitations.statement: General efficient subproblem implementation is not supplied by Algorithm 1. The introduction reports p>=3 implementation as open even in the specified convex optimization special case; the appendix p=2 routine was not read here.

variants.cost: K+1 exact Definition 3.1 subproblem solves, K+1 evaluations F(y_i), and K+1 exact Bregman prox minimizations. Building each Taylor model requires F and derivatives through order p-1 at x_i if these are not encapsulated by the subproblem Oracle. Internal derivative, algebra, subproblem, and prox costs are separately charged and are not bounded here.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.5, Definition 3.1 and Algorithm 1 lines 1–6
variants.name: Exact-subproblem nonzero-step scope
variants.output: Return xhat_K=(sum_{i=0}^K lambda_i y_i)/(sum_{i=0}^K lambda_i), a feasible weighted average of half-step points.
public_inputs: Nonempty closed convex X subset R^n; x_0 in X; integer p>=2; L_p>0; integer K>=0; norm and differentiable prox function d.
variants.query_and_update: For i=0,...,K, form T_{p-1}(u;x_i)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jF(x_i)[u-x_i]^j/j!. Let U_{p,x_i}(u)=T_{p-1}(u;x_i)+(2L_p/p!)omega(u,x_i)^((p-1)/2)(grad d(u)-grad d(x_i)). Query the exact subproblem Oracle for y_i in X satisfying <U_{p,x_i}(y_i),y_i-u><=0 for every u in X. Set lambda_i=(1/2)omega(y_i,x_i)^(-(p-1)/2). Query F(y_i), then set x_{i+1}=argmin_{u in X}{<F(y_i),u-y_i>+L_p omega(u,x_i)/(p!lambda_i)}.
variants.requirements: F:X->R^n is continuous and monotone and has derivatives needed for T_{p-1}; use the Definition 2.6 Taylor remainder bound with L_p. Assume exact solution access for the Definition 3.1 VI and exact Bregman prox minimization. Existence of all requested solutions is an interface requirement; no general implementation theorem is claimed.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize x_0. Define omega(y,x)=d(y)-d(x)-<grad d(x),y-x> and require omega(y,x)>=||y-x||^2. The selected rule applies to runs with positive omega(y_i,x_i) at every executed iteration i=0,...,K.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Execute K+1 iterations. L_p is needed for the subproblem and prox coefficient. No line search appears in this rule. This record supplies no certified epsilon-based stopping budget. If omega(y_i,x_i)=0, the printed negative-power rule is undefined in the selected p>=2 scope; no locally invented termination branch is included.
